claim: AWS Shield Standard protects all AWS customers against common, frequently occurring infrastructure (layer 3 and 4) events such as SYN/UDP floods and reflection events.
question: What does AWS Shield Standard protect against, and who gets it?

values.display: layer 3 and 4
for all AWS customers

evidence.quote: AWS Shield Standard provides protection for all AWS customers against common and most frequently occurring infrastructure (layer 3 and 4) events like SYN/UDP floods, reflection events, and others to support high availability of your applications on AWS.

claim: AWS Shield Standard automatically protects web applications running on AWS against infrastructure layer attacks like UDP floods and state exhaustion attacks like TCP SYN floods.
question: Does AWS Shield Standard need to be turned on?

values.display: automatically provides protection

evidence.quote: AWS Shield Standard automatically provides protection for web applications running on AWS against the most common, frequently occurring Infrastructure layer attacks like UDP floods, and State exhaustion attacks like TCP SYN floods.

claim: Customers can use AWS WAF, alongside AWS Shield Standard, to protect against application layer attacks like HTTP POST or GET floods.
question: What should you add to AWS Shield Standard to protect against HTTP floods?

values.display: HTTP POST or GET floods

evidence.quote: Customers can also use AWS WAF to protect against Application layer attacks like HTTP POST or GET floods.

claim: There are no additional costs for AWS Shield Standard; it is built into the AWS services you already use.
question: How much does AWS Shield Standard cost?

values.display: no additional costs for AWS Shield Standard

evidence.quote: AWS Shield Standard is built into the AWS services that you already use for your web applications.
There are no additional costs for AWS Shield Standard.

claim: There is no limit on the number of resources subject to AWS Shield Standard protection.

values.display: no limit on the number of resources

evidence.quote: There is no limit on the number of resources subject to AWS Shield Standard protection.

claim: AWS Shield Standard is available on all AWS services in every AWS Region and AWS edge location worldwide.

values.display: every AWS Region and AWS edge location

evidence.quote: AWS Shield Standard is available on all AWS services in every AWS Region and AWS edge location worldwide.

claim: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced protections for applications running on protected Amazon EC2, Elastic Load Balancing (ELB), Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator and Route 53 resources against more sophisticated and larger attacks.
question: Which resource types can AWS Shield Advanced protect?

values.display: against more sophisticated and larger attacks

evidence.quote: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced protections for your applications running on protected Amazon EC2, Elastic Load Balancing (ELB), Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator, and Route 53 resources against more sophisticated and larger attacks.

claim: AWS Shield Advanced includes DDoS protection for layers 3, 4 and 7, 24/7 support from the Shield Response Team (SRT), and cost protection against event spikes.
question: What does AWS Shield Advanced add on top of Shield Standard?

values.display: layers 3, 4, and 7
24/7 support from the Shield Response Team

evidence.quote: AWS Shield Advanced includes DDoS protection for layers 3, 4, and 7; 24/7 support from the Shield Response Team (SRT); and cost protection against events spikes.

claim: AWS Shield Advanced customers can enable the AWS WAF application layer DDoS protection feature at no additional cost for up to 50 billion AWS WAF requests per month.
question: How many AWS WAF requests per month are included for AWS Shield Advanced customers using L7 DDoS protection?

values.display: up to 50 billion AWS WAF requests per month

qualifiers.scope: per Shield Advanced customer, per month

claim: AWS Shield Advanced includes DDoS cost protection: if protected resources scale up in response to a DDoS attack, you can request credits through the regular AWS Support channel.
question: How does AWS Shield Advanced handle scaling charges caused by a DDoS attack?

values.display: request credits via the regular AWS Support channel

evidence.quote: AWS Shield Advanced includes DDoS cost protection, a safeguard from scaling charges as a result of a DDoS attack that causes usage spikes on protected Amazon EC2, Elastic Load Balancing (ELB), Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator, or Amazon Route 53.
If any of the AWS Shield Advanced protected resources scale up in response to a DDoS attack, you can request credits via the regular AWS Support channel.

claim: AWS Shield can protect web sites that are not hosted in AWS, because it is integrated with Amazon CloudFront, which supports custom origins outside of AWS.
question: Can AWS Shield protect a web site that is not hosted in AWS?

values.display: supports custom origins outside of AWS

evidence.quote: Yes, AWS Shield is integrated with Amazon CloudFront, which supports custom origins outside of AWS.

claim: To protect resources outside AWS with Shield Advanced, customers put CloudFront or Route 53 in front, protect those with Shield Advanced, and must lock down their backend resources to accept traffic only from these AWS endpoints.
question: What must you do to the origin when you use Shield Advanced on CloudFront in front of resources outside AWS?

values.display: lock down their backend resources

evidence.quote: Customers can then protect these CloudFront distributions and Route 53 hosted zones with Shield Advanced.
Please note that you need to lock down their backend resources to only accept traffic from these AWS endpoints.

claim: You can enable up to 1000 AWS resources of each supported resource type for AWS Shield Advanced protection, and request a limit increase through an AWS Support case for more.
question: How many resources of one type can AWS Shield Advanced protect?

values.display: up to 1000 AWS resources of each supported resource type

evidence.quote: You can enable up to 1000 AWS resources of each supported resource type (Classic / Application Load Balancers, Amazon CloudFront distributions, Amazon Route 53 hosting zones, Elastic IPs, AWS Global Accelerator accelerators) for AWS Shield Advanced protection.
If you want to enable more than 1000, you can request a limit increase by creating an AWS Support case.

claim: You subscribe multiple AWS accounts to AWS Shield Advanced by enabling it on each account, and you pay the monthly fee once if the accounts are under a single consolidated billing and you own all the accounts and their resources.
question: How is AWS Shield Advanced enabled and billed across multiple AWS accounts?

values.display: individually enabling it on each account
You will pay the monthly fee once

evidence.quote: If your organization has multiple AWS accounts, you can subscribe multiple AWS Accounts to AWS Shield Advanced by individually enabling it on each account using the AWS Management Console or API.
You will pay the monthly fee once as long as the AWS accounts are all under a single consolidated billing, and you own all the AWS accounts and resources in those accounts.
